'''Science communication''' encompasses a wide range of activities that connect [[science]] and [[society]].<ref>{{Cite book |title=Communicating science: a global perspective |date=2020 |editor1=Toss Gascoigne |editor2=Bernard Schiele |editor3=Joan Leach |editor4=Michelle Riedlinger |editor5=Bruce V. Lewenstein |editor6=Luisa Massarani |editor7=Peter Broks |publisher=Australian National University Press |isbn=978-1-76046-366-3 |location=Canberra, ACT, Australia |oclc=1184001543}}</ref> Common goals of science communication include informing non-experts about scientific findings, raising the [[Public awareness of science|public awareness of and interest in science]], influencing people's attitudes and behaviors, informing [[public policy]], and [[Public engagement|engaging with diverse communities]] to address societal problems.<ref name=":16">{{Cite book |author1=((National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine)) |author2=Division of Behavioral and Social Sciences and Education |author3=Committee on the Science of Science Communication: A Research Agenda |title=Communicating science effectively: a research agenda |date=2017 |isbn=978-0-309-45103-1 |publisher=National Academies Press |location=Washington, DC |oclc=975003235}}</ref> The term "science communication" generally refers to settings in which audiences are not experts on the scientific topic being discussed ([[Science outreach|outreach]]), though some authors categorize expert-to-expert communication ("inreach" such as [[publication]] in [[scientific journal]]s) as a type of science communication.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Illingworth |first1=Sam |last2=Allen |first2=Grant |date=2020 |orig-date=2016 |chapter=Introduction |title=Effective science communication: a practical guide to surviving as a scientist |edition=2nd |location=Bristol, UK; Philadelphia |publisher=[[IOP Publishing]] |pages=1–5 |isbn=978-0-7503-2518-9 |oclc=1172776633 |doi=10.1088/978-0-7503-2520-2ch1 |doi-access=free |quote=This chapter provides a clearer distinction between the two aspects of science communication that are discussed in this book: that which is aimed at engaging scientists (inward-facing) and that which is aimed at engaging non-scientists (outward-facing).}}</ref> Examples of outreach include [[science journalism]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Anderson |first1=Josh |last2=Dudo |first2=Anthony |date=February 2023 |title=A View From the Trenches: Interviews With Journalists About Reporting Science News |url=http://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/10755470221149156 |journal=Science Communication |language=en |volume=45 |issue=1 |pages=39–64 |doi=10.1177/10755470221149156 |s2cid=256159505 |issn=1075-5470|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-23 |title=How Science News does science journalism {{!}} Science News |url=https://www.sciencenews.org/about-science-news/journalism-standards-practices |access-date=2023-04-09 |language=en-US}}</ref> and [[health communication]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.nap.edu/catalog/25881 |title=Encouraging Adoption of Protective Behaviors to Mitigate the Spread of COVID-19: Strategies for Behavior Change |date=2020-07-23 |publisher=National Academies Press |isbn=978-0-309-68101-8 |location=Washington, D.C. |doi=10.17226/25881|bibcode=2020nap..book25881N |s2cid=241252994 }}</ref> Since science has political, moral, and legal implications,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Scheufele |first=Dietram A. |date=2014-09-16 |title=Science communication as political communication |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=111 |issue=supplement_4 |pages=13585–13592 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1317516111 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=4183176 |pmid=25225389 |doi-access=free }}</ref> science communication can help bridge gaps between different stakeholders in public policy, industry, and civil society <ref name="JensenGerber2020">{{Cite journal |last1=Jensen |first1=Eric A. |last2=Gerber |first2=Alexander |date=2020 |title=Evidence-Based Science Communication |journal=Frontiers in Communication |language=English |volume=4 |article-number=78 |doi=10.3389/fcomm.2019.00078 |issn=2297-900X |doi-access=free}} [[File:CC-BY_icon.svg|50x50px]] Text was copied from this source, which is available under a [[creativecommons:by/4.0/|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].</ref> with trust-building playing a central role in this process.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Curtis |first1=Caitlin |title=Teaching Science Students to Communicate: A Practical Guide |last2=Gillespie |first2=Nicole |last3=Okimoto |first3=Tyler |publisher=SpringerNature |year=2023 |pages=39–47 |chapter=Establishing Trust in Science Communication |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-91628-2_5 |isbn=978-3-030-91627-5 |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-91628-2_5}}</ref>

{{Science|expanded=Society}}
'''Science communicators'''<!--boldface per [[WP:R#PLA]]--> are a broad group of people: scientific experts, science journalists, science artists, [[Health professional|medical professionals]], [[nature center]] educators, science advisors for policymakers, and everyone else who communicates with the public about science.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Build Trust in Science for a Better Future |url=https://www.associationofsciencecommunicators.org/sign-our-open-letter-build-trust-in-science/ |access-date=2023-04-09 |website=Association of Science Communicators |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=About |url=https://www.associationofsciencecommunicators.org/about/ |access-date=2023-04-09 |website=Association of Science Communicators |language=en-US}}</ref> They often use [[entertainment]] and [[persuasion]] techniques including [[humour]], [[storytelling]], and [[metaphors]] to connect with their audience's values and interests.<ref name=POIOlson/><ref name=Krulwich/><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Dudo |first1=Anthony |last2=Besley |first2=John C. |title=What it means to 'know your audience' when communicating about science |url=http://theconversation.com/what-it-means-to-know-your-audience-when-communicating-about-science-111147 |access-date=2023-04-09 |website=The Conversation |date=16 April 2019 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dahlstrom |first=Michael F. |date=2014-09-16 |title=Using narratives and storytelling to communicate science with nonexpert audiences |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=111 |issue=supplement_4 |pages=13614–13620 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1320645111 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=4183170 |pmid=25225368 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

Historically, academic scientists were discouraged from spending time on public outreach, but that has begun to change. Research funders have raised their expectations for researchers to have broader impacts beyond publication in academic journals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Broader Impacts |url=https://beta.nsf.gov/funding/learn/broader-impacts |access-date=2023-04-09 |website=NSF - National Science Foundation |language=en}}</ref> An increasing number of scientists, especially younger scholars, are expressing interest in engaging the public through social media and in-person events, though they still perceive significant institutional barriers to doing so.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rose |first1=Kathleen M. |last2=Markowitz |first2=Ezra M. |last3=Brossard |first3=Dominique |date=2020-01-21 |title=Scientists' incentives and attitudes toward public communication |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=117 |issue=3 |pages=1274–1276 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1916740117 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=6985784 |pmid=31911470 |bibcode=2020PNAS..117.1274R |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Calice |first1=Mikhaila N. |last2=Beets |first2=Becca |last3=Bao |first3=Luye |last4=Scheufele |first4=Dietram A. |last5=Freiling |first5=Isabelle |last6=Brossard |first6=Dominique |last7=Feinstein |first7=Noah Weeth |last8=Heisler |first8=Laura |last9=Tangen |first9=Travis |last10=Handelsman |first10=Jo |date=2022-06-15 |editor-last=Baert |editor-first=Stijn |title=Public engagement: Faculty lived experiences and perspectives underscore barriers and a changing culture in academia |journal=PLOS ONE|language=en |volume=17 |issue=6 |article-number=e0269949 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0269949 |issn=1932-6203 |pmc=9200360 |pmid=35704652 |bibcode=2022PLoSO..1769949C |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":02">{{Cite journal |last=Sha |first=Mandy |date=2025-03-02 |title=Expanding the Reach of Scientific Communication: Tools, Motivation, and Recommendations |url=https://www.surveypractice.org/article/127308-expanding-the-reach-of-scientific-communication-tools-motivation-and-recommendations |journal=Survey Practice |language=en |volume=19 Special Issue |pages=1–8 |doi=10.29115/SP-2024-0032 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
